archetype.name: Game Manager (short-area backup)
archetype.definition: A low-aDOT spot starter who wins by completing the short, schemed throws Ben Johnson's offense hands him and loses when he has to push the ball into the intermediate middle.

report.headline: Steady underneath, shaky between 10 and 19 yards: a capable stopgap, nothing more
report.take:
Bagent is the Bears' QB2, pressed into action because Caleb Williams is out with a hamstring strain. Over three appearances he has looked like the same quarterback he was as a rookie in 2023. He completes a lot of short passes, rarely pushes the ball downfield and doesn't finish drives. His intended air yards (6.02) and career aDOT (6.2) are nearly identical. His throws land almost two yards short of the sticks on average. That is a quarterback playing inside the structure, not creating outside it. His 65.6% completion rate ranks 18th, but it sits beside a passing EPA that ranks 34th and an adjusted net yards per dropback that ranks 40th.

The season splits cleanly in two. On throws of 0-9 yards he has been genuinely good: +0.23 EPA per play, a 62% success rate and a 72% completion rate. On throws of 10-19 yards he has been a liability: 41% completions, 13.8 points below expected, and all three of his interceptions. One change from his rookie year may explain it. His aggressiveness, the share of throws into tight windows, has roughly doubled from 12.6% to 25.45%. That reads like a backup trying to make the throws a starter makes, and the intermediate window is where it is costing him.

Two numbers mislead. First, his pressure-to-sack rate of 40% ranks 34th of 36, but he has been pressured on only 7.6% of dropbacks. That works out to a couple of sacks on a handful of pressured plays. In 2023 he ranked 4th in this stat, so it is noise, not a pocket flaw. Second, zero touchdowns on 64 attempts is partly bad luck and partly who he is. The red zone has been ugly: 46.7% completions and -0.339 EPA on 16 plays. But in 2023 he managed only three TDs across 859 yards, so the floor here is low even after regression.

The game-by-game path is two different quarterbacks. Against the Jets he went 25/34 for 268 yards and +7.9 EPA, with a lot of easy completions. At Green Bay he went 12/21 for 87 yards with two interceptions and -10.3 EPA, and he played only 67% of snaps in a 31-7 loss. Which version shows up depends heavily on how long the game lets him stay underneath. In any case, Williams being 'on track' means this audition may end soon.

strengths.title: Efficient short-area distributor
strengths.body: Inside 10 yards he completes 72% with positive CPOE and a 62% success rate. That is the bread and butter of a Johnson offense that ranks 9th in success rate. His short-throw accuracy matches his 2023 completion percentage, so it is a stable trait.

strengths.title: Gets the ball out cleanly
strengths.body: He has been pressured on only 7.6% of dropbacks, 3rd-lowest among qualifiers. Some of that is a Bears line that ranks 7th in hit rate allowed. Some of it is his own quick, short game. His 2023 pressure-to-sack rate ranked 4th, so the ugly 2026 figure on a handful of pressured snaps should correct.

strengths.title: Odunze connection works
strengths.body: Rome Odunze has returned +0.587 EPA per target on 12 looks, by far his best pairing. When Bagent does push the ball, it tends to be Odunze winning. The deep sample (5 attempts, +0.774 EPA) is too small to trust but points the same way.

concerns.title: Intermediate throws produce the turnovers
concerns.body: On 17 throws of 10-19 yards he has 41% completions, a -13.8 CPOE and all three interceptions. His aggressiveness has jumped from 12.6% in 2023 to 25.45%, so he is forcing tight-window throws in exactly the range where his accuracy falls off. This is a real flaw, not just a role product, though the 17-throw sample exaggerates its size.

concerns.title: Drives stall in the red zone
concerns.body: He has zero TDs on 64 attempts, ranking 42nd of 43 in TD rate. In the red zone he has completed 46.7% at -0.339 EPA per play. Some of that will regress upward, but a 6-yard-aDOT passer who threw three TDs as a rookie starter doesn't carry a high touchdown ceiling.

concerns.title: Loveland targets are dead plays
concerns.body: Colston Loveland has drawn 14 targets at -0.588 EPA per target, tied for Bagent's most-used option and his least productive. Funneling looks to a tight end who isn't producing with him drags the whole passing game, and Atlanta is stingy against tight ends.

trend.note: He was efficient in relief vs. Minnesota's top-ranked defense on nine throws, then had a +7.9 EPA full game against the Jets. That was followed by a -10.3 EPA, two-interception outing at Green Bay in which he played only 67% of snaps. No steady direction, just wide game-to-game swings.

nextGame.headline: If Williams sits, Atlanta's sound defense tests Bagent's short game
nextGame.body:
Atlanta's defense is built to beat his profile. It ranks 3rd in success rate allowed and 5th in EPA allowed on short throws, the area Bagent depends on. It also ranks 5th against deep passes, so there is no easy vertical relief. The QB-friendly 'allows 18.9 PPR a game' figure (24th) is mostly volume. Offenses pass 6.6 points more than normal against Atlanta, the strongest pass funnel in the league, because its run defense holds up. Volume will be there, efficiency probably won't. The soft spot is the WR2 role (+0.51 EPA per play, 25th), and Odunze or Burden should get chances there.

Availability drives everything. Williams is listed Out with an estimated return of game day, and Johnson called Atlanta or later a coin flip. If Williams returns, Bagent likely doesn't take a meaningful snap. Kyle Monangai, a 41%-snap back, is out, which thins the run game Bagent leans on. On Atlanta's side, Za'Darius Smith (out) and Yasir Abdullah (IR) are part-time pieces, and CB C.J. Henderson (66% of snaps) is questionable. Henderson's absence would help the outside throws. Michael Penix Jr.'s rib injury could also blunt Atlanta's already 27th-ranked passing offense. That keeps this a low-possession game, and I'd lean to the under on a 49.5 total that sits above every Bears total so far, all three of which went under. The roof is retractable and the forecast is early, so weather shouldn't factor.

keyMatchups.title: Short game vs. stingy underneath defense
keyMatchups.body: Bagent's offense lives on 0-9 yard completions, and Atlanta allows only -0.104 EPA on short throws. If those plays are only marginally successful, he gets pushed into the intermediate range where his interceptions come from.

keyMatchups.title: Attack the WR2 spot
keyMatchups.body: Atlanta has given up +0.51 EPA per play and 3.2 PPR over average to opposing WR2s. That is the clearest hole in an otherwise solid defense, and a Henderson absence would widen it.

keyMatchups.title: Pass-funnel volume, little efficiency
keyMatchups.body: Teams throw against Atlanta more than any other defense relative to situation. Johnson's Bears lean run (-3.1 pass rate over expected), but a stout Falcons front plus no Monangai could force more dropbacks onto Bagent than he usually gets.

nextGame.watch: Whether Williams is cleared. If Bagent starts, watch his throws between 10 and 19 yards, where all of his turnovers have come.

restOfSeason.body: The likeliest path is a return to the bench once Williams is healthy, so the rest of his season is probably spot duty. In any start, expect what he has always been: a mid-60s completion rate, around 6 yards per attempt and a low aDOT. Volume and efficiency will swing on game script. The zero-touchdown rate will normalize somewhat, and the inflated pressure-to-sack rate should fall back toward his 2023 level. The intermediate interceptions will ease if he goes back to his rookie-year caution. What won't change is a modest ceiling: he isn't a quarterback who lifts an offense, he keeps it on schedule.
swingFactors: Timing of Caleb Williams' hamstring return
Whether his tight-window aggressiveness settles back toward 2023 levels
Monangai's return and the run game's support

confidence.note: 64 attempts across three uneven appearances, and his starting role hinges on Williams' hamstring.
